title: Image of a closed subset proper over a base under a universally closed morphism
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$ be morphisms locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism over $S$ which is universally closed [def-weil-proper-morphism]. If $Z\subseteq X$ is a closed subset proper over $S$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base], then $f(Z)$ is a closed subset of $Y$ and it is proper over $S$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0CYQ (lemma-functoriality-closed-proper-over-base) part (2) and the proof of (2)

proof.text: Give $Z$ and $Z'=f(Z)$ their reduced induced closed subscheme structures [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. The inclusion of the underlying image gives a morphism $Z\to Z'$ over $S$. Let $Z''=X\times_Y Z'$ be the scheme-theoretic inverse image of $Z'$ in $X$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Since $Z$ is reduced and its image is contained in the closed subscheme $Z''\to X$, [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] (Stacks Schemes 0356) gives the factorization $Z\to Z''$. The map $Z''\to Z'$ is the base change of $f$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0CYQ (lemma-functoriality-closed-proper-over-base), proof of (2), first two sentences

proof.text: The base-change projection $Z''\to Z'$ is universally closed by [lem-weil-pbc-universally-closed-base-change] (Stacks Morphisms 01W4). The map $Z\to Z''$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-cancellation] (Stacks Morphisms 07RK): $Z\to X$ is a closed immersion and $Z''\to X$ is separated, being a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Hence $Z\to Z'$ is universally closed, using [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc] (f) for composition. It is surjective because its underlying image is $f(Z)=Z'$.

proof.text: The structure morphism $Z\to S$ is proper by the hypothesis that $Z$ is proper over $S$, hence separated and universally closed [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Since $Z\to Z'$ is surjective and universally closed, [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-universally-closed-separated] implies that $Z'\to S$ is separated.

proof.text: The map $Z'\to S$ is locally of finite type: the closed immersion Z' into Y is proper and therefore locally of finite type [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (c), while $Y\to S$ is locally of finite type by hypothesis, so the composite is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (e).

proof.text: The proper morphism $Z\to S$ is universally closed, and $Z\to Z'$ is surjective. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-image-universally-closed] (Stacks Morphisms 03GN) to this factorization shows that $Z'\to S$ is universally closed; together with the separatedness and local finite type from the preceding steps, it is proper. Its underlying image in $Y$ is the closed subset $Z'$, so $f(Z)$ is closed and proper over $S$.

split_report.summary: Split the proof of Stacks Cohomology of Schemes Lemma 0CYQ (tag 0CYQ), part (2), into five steps. The reduced structures on Z and f(Z), the scheme-theoretic inverse image Z'' and the factorization Z -> Z'' follow the fibre-product and reduced-closed-subscheme nodes, with the reduced-source factorization cited explicitly as Schemes 0356. Z'' -> Z' uses the new Mathlib leaf for base-change stability of universal closedness (Stacks Morphisms 01W4, Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.universallyClosed_isStableUnderBaseChange at UniversallyClosed.lean:65). The closed immersion Z -> Z'' is now cited through the exact closed-immersion cancellation node for Stacks Morphisms 07RK and Mathlib IsClosedImmersion.of_comp. Composition with the closed immersion gives a surjective universally closed Z -> Z', then existing 09MQ separatedness descent and 03GN image-universally-closed yield that Z' -> S is separated, locally of finite type, universally closed, hence proper. The target image is therefore the closed subset f(Z)=Z' proper over S.
